# Tasmota Scan & Control

> Free, open-source (GPL-3.0) Android app to find, switch and schedule Tasmota and Shelly Wi-Fi switches, plugs and lamps on your own network. No cloud, no account, no ads, no device limit. Made by Dirk Lubèrth Dijkman, together with Claude Opus 5.5.

Key facts:

- Platform: Android 7.0 or newer. Adding a brand-new device from the app needs Android 10 or newer. No iPhone version; a browser demo is available.
- License: GNU GPL-3.0, source code on GitHub.
- Price: free. No ads, no in-app purchases, no subscription, no limit on the number of devices, groups, scenes or widgets.
- Works with any device running Tasmota firmware (ESP8266/ESP32: Sonoff, Athom, plugs, relays, wall switches, lamps, LED strips). OpenBeken partly works (switching yes, schedules no). Shelly devices work fully when they run Tasmota. Shelly devices with their own firmware (Gen1 and Plus/Pro/Gen3/Gen4) are found by the scan and can be switched on and off, renamed and given an auto-off. Tested on a real Shelly 1 Gen3 (firmware 1.4.0 and 2.2.0): adding it to the home Wi-Fi from the app, switching, auto-off, schedules, the one-tap firmware update (1.4.0 to 2.2.0), temperature, and the access point / Bluetooth / MQTT status. Gen2+ Shelly cards show Wi-Fi signal, uptime, firmware version with a one-tap update when a new version is available, the device temperature, red warnings (overheating, overload, over/under voltage), and whether the Shelly's own access point (AP), Bluetooth and MQTT are on; an open AP without password shows in red, and AP or Bluetooth can be turned off with one tap. Schedules work on Shelly Gen2 and newer: the same 8 on/off schedule cards with sunrise/sunset become Shelly schedule jobs, stored in the Shelly itself (cards in the Shelly KVS, so every phone and wall panel sees them). Shelly bulbs and dimmers (Gen2 and newer, e.g. Duo Bulb Gen3 and Multicolor Bulb Gen3, and Gen1 Duo/Vintage) get brightness, white (2700–6500 K) and colour in the same light window as Tasmota lamps. Not yet tested on real hardware: Shelly bulbs, Shelly home screen widgets and Gen1 Shellys. Energy (watts, kWh) for Shelly is not supported yet; a Shelly 1PM Gen3 and Gen4 are on their way for testing.
- Local only: the app talks directly to the devices over the local Wi-Fi, via Tasmota's HTTP API and Shelly's local RPC API. No cloud server, no MQTT broker needed, no tracking.
- Signing key: since version 24.2 (21 November 2026) the APK is signed with a new private key using APK key rotation (v3). Android 9+ moves to the new key on a normal in-app update; Android 7/8 keep the old key. If an update ever fails with "App not installed", uninstall and reinstall. New key SHA-256: CC:CD:AD:B9:A4:93:64:70:08:91:98:5A:CC:B4:49:F7:81:3A:DF:56:78:E5:5C:C3:53:9F:08:5D:D6:18:B5:24. Only download from github.com/ldijkman/Tasmota-android-test. The app (package nl.dijkman.plafondled) is registered with Google's Android developer verification (21 November 2026), so it stays normally installable on certified Android devices when verification is enforced. The registered key is the new key (Android 9 and newer). Android 7/8 phones still recognise the app by the old key, which is not registered; what that means for them will be decided when enforcement reaches Europe (expected 2027). The website shows a "Registered developer" badge under the Download button; it is the developer's own badge, not a Google certification.
- Not in the Play Store: the app is made by one person in his spare time, and a new Play Store app needs a fee, an identity check and first 12 testers for 14 days. The APK is built by GitHub Actions from the public source code and downloaded from GitHub Releases. Updates install from inside the app (Check for update, at the bottom of the main screen).
- APK size: under 250 KB.
- Works side by side with the official Shelly app: both can control the same Shelly, and switching, auto-off and schedules are stored in the Shelly itself. The Shelly app works with every Shelly and only with Shelly, also away from home and with Alexa or Google Home, and needs a Shelly account; this app is smaller, needs no account, stays local and shows Tasmota and Shelly switches on one screen. Note: this app makes schedules as on/off pairs (one on time and one off time per schedule), so schedules made in the Shelly app may not show up in this app, but they keep working in the Shelly.

Features:

- Network scan that finds all Tasmota devices (and Shelly devices) in seconds; recognises devices by MAC address when their IP changes.
- On/off/toggle, groups (rooms), scenes (several switches with one tap), big tiles screen.
- Scenes on a 2-wide grid with free placement and empty spaces; own colours per scene for icon, name and border. After running a scene, the result (e.g. "3 of 3 done", or which switch was not reachable) shows on the scene tile itself.
- Up to 8 on/off schedules per switch with fixed times or sunrise/sunset with offset, stored and run in the switch itself (they keep working with the phone off).
- Lamps: brightness, white colour temperature, colour.
- Auto-off after a set time (Tasmota PulseTime, Shelly auto-off); also works when the physical button on the device is pressed. Tap the auto-off line on a card ("off in 58:16" or "auto-off 30 min") to jump straight to the auto-off setting.
- Energy use (watts) for plugs with a power meter.
- Sensor values on the card: temperature, humidity, air pressure, light, CO2, distance (e.g. AM2301, DS18B20, BME280).
- Per card, optional: Wi-Fi signal and uptime, last restart reason (crashes shown in orange), Tasmota version and chip. Tap the IP address to open the device's own Tasmota web page.
- Drag to reorder switches and whole groups.
- Home screen widgets for switches, groups, scenes, Wi-Fi and Tailscale.
- Add a new or reset device from the menu, without the browser: "Add new Tasmota" (the device's tasmota-… Wi-Fi), and "Add new Shelly" (Gen1, Gen2, Gen3, Gen4; tested on a real Shelly 1 Gen3). The app gives it the home Wi-Fi, a name and the location, and on Gen2+ turns off the Shelly's own setup access point afterwards.
- Wall panel (kiosk) mode for a spare phone or tablet: keep screen on, dim after a set time, full screen, use as home screen app, black OLED theme.
- Remote control from anywhere with Tailscale (a phone or tablet at home acts as subnet router; no ports opened on the router).
- Seven themes, share setup to another phone, own icons and colours, built-in farm and pet animal icons.
- Open the app from a web page with tasmotascan:// links (tasmotascan://open, ://scenes, ://tiles).
